  "body": "I see only the body of the selected account, p.rival.0; its commitments were withheld, so I am rivalling the visible pose rather than anything it may have staked.

That account reads the situation as failing governance: agreements are underspecified, no routine exists for revising them as schedules move, and one member is withdrawing from the forum. Its remedies refine the collective mechanism — write agreements down, hold a standing review, assign zones of ownership, soften re-entry for the avoider. This rival inverts the diagnosis: the flat is over-coordinated, not under-coordinated. Three people with diverging standards, schedules and willingness are being asked to govern too much jointly, and the fights are the friction of that load. The remedy is therefore not better agreements but fewer of them — shrink the surface the household must manage together.

Rival reading of the meaning fights. The selected account's main conjecture is specification drift, fixable by writing things down. Mine: repeated 'what did we agree' fights are how an unresolved grievance — about standards, effort or respect — gets re-litigated when it cannot be addressed directly. If that is right, recording agreements migrates the dispute rather than settling it: 'you said' becomes 'what the note meant', plus fresh arguments about exceptions and enforcement. Written records under low trust become ammunition rather than closure. The reading is falsifiable: if disputes genuinely drop once recording begins, my conjecture is wrong; if they recur in textual form at a similar rate, the specification fix was treating a symptom.

The avoider belongs at the centre, not as one of three braided faults. Withdrawal is the most diagnostic fact in the task: it says the conversation itself has become a cost someone has stopped paying. Everything the selected account prescribes requires more or better-formatted participation — a standing review, one-on-ones, shared note-keeping — which is structurally tuned to the people already in the room, not the person leaving it. Under the rival pose, any fix must cut the participation demanded of the avoider, not merely smooth the demand.

What follows for intervention. Change the object of governance before improving the governor. (1) Privatize what can be privatized: own dishes, own laundry, own shelves, own room. What remains genuinely common — bins, bathroom, shared surfaces — gets one thin rule, and only that residue needs any of the selected account's machinery. (2) Outsource what can be bought: a cleaner every week or fortnight, split three ways, converts the largest recurring conflict into a fixed cost; affordability is unknowable from the task text and decides how much of the problem is purchasable. (3) Lower the shared standard deliberately: accept asymmetry — each private zone held to its owner's standard, shared zones to a negotiated minimum rather than the highest member's. That is a values choice, not a defect. (4) Declare a truce on enforcing past agreements for a period; the holding-to-account is itself the friction, and a moratorium de-escalates without adjudicating anything. (5) If conflict persists after all that, treat the configuration as the variable: the flat-share and the friendship are two relationships currently governed as one, and someone moving out — or the group agreeing to cohabit without cooperating — is a legitimate remedy that protects the friendship by ending the governance relationship. Exit reframed as repair, not failure.

One conversation, different agenda. The selected account prescribes a standing review; the rival prescribes a single short exchange — sized to what the avoider will actually attend, possibly one-on-one or in writing — whose only question is: how do we arrange things so we need far fewer of these conversations? The difference matters. One frames the household as a body to be better managed; the other as a load to be reduced.

Honest weaknesses of this pose. At least three. First, privatization cannot cover the true commons; if standards diverge badly, even bins and bathroom sustain a war, and an enforcement truce may let everything settle at the lowest member's level. Second, if chores really do proxy for care and respect, as the selected account also conjectures, then decoupling can be read as 'I have given up on you' and worsen the relationship precisely by succeeding at the chores; the mitigation is to frame every decoupling proposal explicitly as friendship-protecting and to keep a few deliberately shared rituals. Third, the asker's lever shrinks under this pose: they can unilaterally privatize their own sphere and propose the rest, but they cannot make the others prefer peace over fairness.

Tests that discriminate the frames cheaply, before committing to either: offer written agreements and watch whether the reaction is relief (specification was binding) or suspicion about who checks (trust was binding); propose privatization or a cleaner and watch for instant enthusiasm; watch whether the avoider re-engages once the demanded participation shrinks. Two to four weeks of this tells more than another summit.

Open questions under this pose: whether the household values fairness-in-effort or peace more — the right frame depends on that weighting, and the three may weight it differently; whether the avoider intends to stay in the flat at all — if exit is already in motion, repair should target the relationship, not the chores; and whether a specific incident triggered the spiral — if so, repairing that incident outranks any structural change, on either pose.

The poses are partially combinable: after privatization shrinks the commons, written notes and a default swap rule can govern what remains. The rivalry is about which lever is primary and how the avoidance is read, not about exclusivity.",

This rival poses the same facts as over-coordination across diverging standards and willingness; the disputes are friction from governing too much jointly, not a specification defect.","scope":"competing primary-fault diagnosis"},{"id":"r2","type":"claim","text":"Recurring fights over what was agreed can be re-litigations of an unresolved fairness, standards or respect grievance; if so, recording agreements migrates the dispute from memory to text interpretation, exceptions and enforcement rather than ending it.","grounds":"conjecture, discriminated by whether disputes persist in textual form after recording begins"},{"id":"r3","type":"objection","text":"Writing agreements into a shared place presumes enforcement trust; under low trust the record becomes ammunition and each note a new disputed surface.","bearing":"

Work on the problem using the material actually exposed in this request and your background knowledge. The problem has no supplied answer key or scoring rule. Claims, criticisms and methods are fallible. Do not invent a source, an observation, an earlier event, or a dependency to fill a field. A missing view says what you can currently see; it does not establish what happened earlier. Return a JSON object with exactly two independently authored string fields: body and commitments. Body is your public prose contribution. Commitments says what taking your contribution up would involve. An empty commitment surface is allowed when none can be identified. Do not repeat the body wholesale into commitments.

Use FCL-1 for the commitment surface, encoded as a JSON document inside the commitments string: {"language":"FCL-1","records":[...],"uptake":[...]}. Each record has unique local id, type (claim|commitment|objection|use|problem), and text (unrestricted prose). Optional prose fields: scope, action, consequence, grounds, bearing. Optional arrays of references: target, depends, mentions, revises, withdraws. References are local IDs or exposed-artifact-label#local-ID; do not invent hidden IDs. A commitment proposes a scoped use, action, application or consequence; an objection alleges a defect whose bearing can itself be criticized; a use proposes an uptake or response; a problem states an unresolved question. depends asserts reliance; mentions only locates material. uptake lists the records you currently propose to use, not certified truths. No record type or optional field must be present. Empty records and uptake are allowed. Express uncertainty or an unrepresentable relation in prose rather than inventing a relation. The body remains unrestricted prose.

Return one JSON object with exactly two string fields: "body" and "commitments". Write the actual commitments separately; do not copy the body into that field as a storage shortcut.

# rival

Explore another way of posing or addressing the problem. You see the account's body; its commitment field is not supplied.

## Original problem (task)
[01274f41553299e7] (h005.task.v1)
I share a flat with two friends. We keep arguing about ordinary household chores. Sometimes we agree on who will do something, but later we disagree about what the agreement meant. Our work schedules change, and one friend has started avoiding the conversations. What should I do?

## Selected input account (p.rival.0)

BODY
An account of the problem, built from the task text alone. The selected previous input (p.account.0) exposed no readable content to this invocation, so this begins fresh rather than continuing anything.

The situation contains three separate faults braided together, and separating them matters because they need different handling.

First, meaning drift: agreements get made, then read differently later. My main conjecture is underspecification — "I'll sort the dishes" leaves open by when, how often, and what counts as done, so each person fills the gaps from their own memory and convenience. Worth holding a second conjecture alongside: the ambiguity may be doing work, letting people quietly re-tailor commitments when schedules change, in which case the fight about meaning is really a displaced fight about the changed circumstances.

Second, a moving target: schedules change, so any one-off division of labour decays. Conjecture: the flat has allocations but no allocation mechanism — no routine, low-friction way to revise who does what — so every schedule change forces a fresh full negotiation, and every negotiation is a new chance to argue. If that is right, renegotiating the current split solves nothing durable; the repair has to be at the level of process.

Third, withdrawal: one friend is avoiding the conversations. Conjecture: avoidance is information about the conversation, not only about the chores. Readings that fit: the talks keep turning into disputes about what was said; the avoider expects to lose or to be held later to ambiguities; or their schedule makes any commitment feel like a trap. Any remedy requiring a long three-way summit is structurally mismatched to this fault.

Two weaker conjectures as amplifiers rather than explanations: people reliably notice their own contributions more than others', so all three flatmates may sincerely feel over-burdened; and chore rows often proxy for fairness and respect, so winning an argument rarely settles the feeling. I flag these as speculative — the practical direction below does not depend on them.

What follows for action, conjecturally: (1) recast "what did we agree" fights as specification bugs and write agreements somewhere shared — what, by when, and what done means — turning "you said" into "we wrote"; (2) install a short standing review (fifteen minutes every week or two) so schedule changes get absorbed routinely, with a default rule for missed slots — swap with a named person rather than quietly skip; (3) shrink the negotiable surface by assigning zones or recurring ownership instead of re-deciding task by task; (4) approach the avoider one-on-one, briefly, possibly in writing, asking what would make these exchanges easier rather than why they have been absent; (5) accept that the asker's lever is their own moves — the format they propose and how they respond when a meaning dispute starts — not control of the other two.

Open questions the task text cannot settle, and which a continuer should keep open: whether the avoider is currently doing more or less than their share; whether a specific incident triggered the withdrawal; and whether the three even share a standard of "clean" and "done" — if standards diverge, perfectly recorded agreements will still breed disputes.

## What to return
A JSON object carrying "body" and "commitments". Both are strings and nothing else is required.
